newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada to raise some intl cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada to raise some intl cargo rates.

text.p: Air Canada is raising westbound transatlantic cargo rates by five percent from its two largest continental European gateways, an official said.
The increase takes effect Saturday ex-Paris and April 1 ex-Frankfurt, said marketing manager Gerry Simpson.
Air Canada already announced a five percent domestic rate increase for March 1.
Many ex-North America rates were raised on January 1.
Simpson said these increases still leave Air Canada yields below where they were a year ago when most carriers slashed transatlantic and transpacific rates in response to a market slump.
Separately financially strapped Canadian Airlines International and alliance partner British Airways are aggressively discounting some type of ex-Canada traffic.
Industry sources said the two are offering ex-Canada bellyhold pallet rates of C$1,100, versus C$1,350 for Air Canada - an 18.5% differential - and even more for carriers like Deutsche Lufthansa AG.

In BA's case, the differential appears to reflect market resistance caused by perceived service problems at the carrier's Heathrow hub, the sources said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
